key_insight: Machine-learning models compress quantum measurement data to provide wavefunction overlaps efficiently, accelerating quantum-classical Monte Carlo by orders of magnitude.
engineering_relevance: Reusing quantum-state information through a classical model reduces repeated measurement-processing costs in hybrid quantum simulation workflows.
method: Prepare trial wavefunctions on a quantum processor to guide classical quantum Monte Carlo.
Train machine-learning models to compress quantum measurement data.
Use model-provided wavefunction overlaps during Monte Carlo calculations.
evidence_signal: Using measurements from Google's Willow processor, the study evaluates hydrogen chains and strongly correlated iron-sulfur clusters, reporting chemically accurate simulations on up to 40 qubits.
watch_item: Model-provided overlaps must remain accurate enough to preserve chemical accuracy as system size and correlation complexity grow.
paper_title: Machine learning quantum data to accelerate quantum Monte Carlo
